## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - REQUIRED: Set up isolated workspace before starting

   434→
   435→	// Basic metadata validation
   436→	AssertCheckpointExists(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)
   437→	AssertCheckpointMetadataComplete(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)
   438→
   439→	if v.Strategy != "" {
   440→		meta := ReadCheckpointMetadata(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)
   441→		assert.Equal(t, v.Strategy, meta.Strategy,
   442→			"checkpoint %s: strategy mismatch", v.CheckpointID)
   443→	}
   444→
   445→	if len(v.FilesTouched) > 0 {
   446→		AssertCheckpointFilesTouched(t, dir, v.CheckpointID, v.FilesTouched)
   447→	}
   448→
   449→	path := CheckpointPath(v.CheckpointID)
   450→
   451→	// Validate session metadata exists and has checkpoint_id
   452→	sessionBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/metadata.json", path)
   453→	sessionRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", sessionBlob)
   454→	if assert.NotEmpty(t, sessionRaw, "session metadata should exist at %s", sessionBlob) {
   455→		var sessionMeta map[string]any
   456→		if assert.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(sessionRaw), &sessionMeta)) {
   457→			assert.Equal(t, v.CheckpointID, sessionMeta["checkpoint_id"],
   458→				"session metadata checkpoint_id should match")
   459→			assert.NotEmpty(t, sessionMeta["created_at"], "session metadata should have created_at")
   460→		}
   461→	}
   462→
   463→	// Validate transcript is valid JSONL
   464→	transcriptBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/full.jsonl", path)
   465→	transcriptRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", transcriptBlob)
   466→	if assert.NotEmpty(t, transcriptRaw, "transcript should exist at %s", transcriptBlob) {
   467→		lines := strings.Split(transcriptRaw, "\n")
   468→		validLines := 0
   469→		for i, line := range lines {
   470→			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   471→			if line == "" {
   472→				continue
   473→			}
   474→			validLines++
   475→			var obj map[string]any
   476→			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); err != nil {
   477→				// Log but don't fail — non-Claude agents may have different formats
   478→				t.Logf("transcript line %d is not valid JSON: %v", i+1, err)
   479→			}
   480→		}
   481→		assert.Greater(t, validLines, 0, "transcript should have at least one line")
   482→
   483→		for _, expected := range v.ExpectedTranscriptContent {
   484→			assert.Contains(t, transcriptRaw, expected,
   485→				"transcript should contain %q", expected)
   486→		}
   487→
   488→		// Validate content hash
   489→		hashBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/content_hash.txt", path)
   490→		hashRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", hashBlob)
   491→		if hashRaw != "" {
   492→			hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(transcriptRaw))
   493→			expectedHash := "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])
   494→			assert.Equal(t, expectedHash, strings.TrimSpace(hashRaw),
   495→				"content hash should match transcript SHA-256")
   496→		}
   497→	}
   498→
   499→	// Validate prompt.txt if expected prompts specified
   500→	if len(v.ExpectedPrompts) > 0 {
   501→		promptBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/prompt.txt", path)
   502→		promptRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", promptBlob)
   503→		for _, expected := range v.ExpectedPrompts {
   504→			assert.Contains(t, promptRaw, expected,
   505→				"prompt.txt should contain %q", expected)
   506→		}
   507→	}
   508→}
   509→```

   615→package agents

   627→type openCodeAgent struct {
   628→	model   string
   629→	timeout time.Duration
   630→}
   631→
   632→func init() {
   633→	if _, err := exec.LookPath("opencode"); err != nil {
   634→		return // don't register if not installed
   635→	}
   636→	model := os.Getenv("E2E_OPENCODE_MODEL")
   637→	if model == "" {
   638→		model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
   639→	}
   640→	Register(&openCodeAgent{model: model, timeout: 2 * time.Minute})
   641→}

   643→func (a *openCodeAgent) Name() string            { return "opencode" }
   644→func (a *openCodeAgent) EntireAgent() string      { return "opencode" }
   645→func (a *openCodeAgent) PromptPattern() string    { return `\$` }
   646→func (a *openCodeAgent) TimeoutMultiplier() float64 { return 2.0 }
   647→
   648→func (a *openCodeAgent) RunPrompt(ctx context.Context, dir string, prompt string, opts ...Option) (Output, error) {
   649→	cfg := &runConfig{}
   650→	for _, o := range opts {
   651→		o(cfg)
   652→	}
   653→
   654→	model := a.model
   655→	if cfg.Model != "" {
   656→		model = cfg.Model
   657→	}
   658→
   659→	args := []string{"run"}
   660→	if model != "" {
   661→		args = append(args, "--model", model)
   662→	}
   663→	args = append(args, prompt)
   664→
   665→	timeout := a.timeout
   666→	if envTimeout := os.Getenv("E2E_TIMEOUT"); envTimeout != "" {
   667→		if parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(envTimeout); err == nil {
   668→			timeout = parsed
   669→		}
   670→	}
   671→
   672→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
   673→	defer cancel()
   674→
   675→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "opencode", args...)
   676→	cmd.Dir = dir
   677→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0")
   678→
   679→	var stdout, stderr strings.Builder
   680→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   681→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   682→
   683→	err := cmd.Run()
   684→	out := Output{
   685→		Command: fmt.Sprintf("opencode %s", strings.Join(args, " ")),
   686→		Stdout:  stdout.String(),
   687→		Stderr:  stderr.String(),
   688→	}
   689→
   690→	if err != nil {
   691→		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
   692→		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
   693→			out.ExitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
   694→		} else {
   695→			out.ExitCode = -1
   696→		}
   697→		return out, err
   698→	}
   699→
   700→	return out, nil
   701→}
   702→
   703→func (a *openCodeAgent) StartSession(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Session, error) {
   704→	return nil, fmt.Errorf("opencode: interactive sessions not supported")
   705→}

```go
package tests

import (
	"context"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/entire-io/e2e-tests/testutil"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

// TestEndedSessionUserCommitsAfterExit tests that after an agent session ends
// naturally, user commits still get checkpoint trailers. This exercises the
// session ENDED + user commit path.
func TestEndedSessionUserCommitsAfterExit(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		// Agent creates 3 files — session ends when agent exits
```

```go
// TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion tests that deleting a file that was tracked

func TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		// Pre-seed a file that the agent will delete
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
			filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"),
			[]byte("package main\n\nfunc ToDelete() {}\n"), 0o644))
		s.Git(t, "add", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", "Add to_delete.go")

		// Agent deletes it and creates a replacement
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Do two things: (1) Delete the file to_delete.go using rm. "+
				"(2) Create a new file replacement.go with content 'package main; func Replacement() {}'. "+
				"Do both tasks. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		// to_delete.go should be gone, replacement.go should exist
		assert.NoFileExists(t, filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"))
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "replacement.go")

		// Commit the replacement file
		s.Git(t, "add", "replacement.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add replacement")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID1 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID1)

		cpBranchAfterFirst := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		// Commit the deletion via git rm
		s.Git(t, "rm", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Remove to_delete.go")

		// Check if deletion got a checkpoint — this is soft validation
		// (deleted files may or may not carry forward depending on CLI behavior)
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterDeletion := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
		if cpBranchAfterDeletion != cpBranchAfterFirst {
			cpID2 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
			assert.NotEqual(t, cpID1, cpID2, "checkpoint IDs should be distinct")
			t.Logf("deletion commit got checkpoint %s (carry-forward)", cpID2)
		} else {
			t.Log("deletion commit has no checkpoint (deleted files may not carry forward)")
		}
	})
```

```go
// ValidateCheckpointDeep performs comprehensive validation of checkpoint metadata
// on the checkpoint branch, including transcript JSONL validity, content hash
// verification, and prompt content checking.
func ValidateCheckpointDeep(t *testing.T, dir string, v DeepCheckpointValidation) {
	t.Helper()

	// Basic metadata validation
	AssertCheckpointExists(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)
	AssertCheckpointMetadataComplete(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)

	if v.Strategy != "" {
		meta := ReadCheckpointMetadata(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)
		assert.Equal(t, v.Strategy, meta.Strategy,
			"checkpoint %s: strategy mismatch", v.CheckpointID)
	}

	if len(v.FilesTouched) > 0 {
		AssertCheckpointFilesTouched(t, dir, v.CheckpointID, v.FilesTouched)
	}

	path := CheckpointPath(v.CheckpointID)

	// Validate session metadata exists and has checkpoint_id
	sessionBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/metadata.json", path)
	sessionRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", sessionBlob)
	if assert.NotEmpty(t, sessionRaw, "session metadata should exist at %s", sessionBlob) {
		var sessionMeta map[string]any
		if assert.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(sessionRaw), &sessionMeta)) {
			assert.Equal(t, v.CheckpointID, sessionMeta["checkpoint_id"],
				"session metadata checkpoint_id should match")
			assert.NotEmpty(t, sessionMeta["created_at"], "session metadata should have created_at")
		}
	}

	// Validate transcript is valid JSONL
	transcriptBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/full.jsonl", path)
	transcriptRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", transcriptBlob)
	if assert.NotEmpty(t, transcriptRaw, "transcript should exist at %s", transcriptBlob) {
		lines := strings.Split(transcriptRaw, "\n")
		validLines := 0
		for i, line := range lines {
			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
			if line == "" {
				continue
			}
			validLines++
			var obj map[string]any
			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); err != nil {
				// Log but don't fail — non-Claude agents may have different formats
				t.Logf("transcript line %d is not valid JSON: %v", i+1, err)
			}
		}
		assert.Greater(t, validLines, 0, "transcript should have at least one line")

		for _, expected := range v.ExpectedTranscriptContent {
			assert.Contains(t, transcriptRaw, expected,
				"transcript should contain %q", expected)
		}

		// Validate content hash
		hashBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/content_hash.txt", path)
		hashRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", hashBlob)
		if hashRaw != "" {
			hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(transcriptRaw))
			expectedHash := "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])
			assert.Equal(t, expectedHash, strings.TrimSpace(hashRaw),
				"content hash should match transcript SHA-256")
		}
	}

	// Validate prompt.txt if expected prompts specified
	if len(v.ExpectedPrompts) > 0 {
		promptBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/prompt.txt", path)
		promptRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", promptBlob)
		for _, expected := range v.ExpectedPrompts {
			assert.Contains(t, promptRaw, expected,
				"prompt.txt should contain %q", expected)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package agents

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

type openCodeAgent struct {
	model   string
	timeout time.Duration
}

func init() {
	if _, err := exec.LookPath("opencode"); err != nil {
		return // don't register if not installed
	}
	model := os.Getenv("E2E_OPENCODE_MODEL")
	if model == "" {
		model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
	}
	Register(&openCodeAgent{model: model, timeout: 2 * time.Minute})
}

func (a *openCodeAgent) Name() string            { return "opencode" }
func (a *openCodeAgent) EntireAgent() string      { return "opencode" }
func (a *openCodeAgent) PromptPattern() string    { return `\$` }
func (a *openCodeAgent) TimeoutMultiplier() float64 { return 2.0 }

func (a *openCodeAgent) RunPrompt(ctx context.Context, dir string, prompt string, opts ...Option) (Output, error) {
	cfg := &runConfig{}
	for _, o := range opts {
		o(cfg)
	}

	model := a.model
	if cfg.Model != "" {
		model = cfg.Model
	}

	args := []string{"run"}
	if model != "" {
		args = append(args, "--model", model)
	}
	args = append(args, prompt)

	timeout := a.timeout
	if envTimeout := os.Getenv("E2E_TIMEOUT"); envTimeout != "" {
		if parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(envTimeout); err == nil {
			timeout = parsed
		}
	}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
	defer cancel()

	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "opencode", args...)
	cmd.Dir = dir
	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0")

	var stdout, stderr strings.Builder
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
	cmd.Stderr = &stderr

	err := cmd.Run()
	out := Output{
		Command: fmt.Sprintf("opencode %s", strings.Join(args, " ")),
		Stdout:  stdout.String(),
		Stderr:  stderr.String(),
	}

	if err != nil {
		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
			out.ExitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
		} else {
			out.ExitCode = -1
		}
		return out, err
	}

	return out, nil
}

func (a *openCodeAgent) StartSession(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Session, error) {
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("opencode: interactive sessions not supported")
}
```

    18→// SkipKnownIssue skips the test with a known-issue reference unless

    20→func SkipKnownIssue(t *testing.T, issue, reason string) {
    21→	t.Helper()
    22→	if os.Getenv("E2E_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES") != "" {
    23→		t.Logf("running known issue %s (E2E_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES set): %s", issue, reason)
    24→		return

    29→// AssertFileExists asserts that at least one file matches the glob pattern

    31→func AssertFileExists(t *testing.T, dir string, glob string) {
    32→	t.Helper()
    33→	matches, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, glob))
    34→	require.NoError(t, err)
    35→	assert.NotEmpty(t, matches, "expected files matching %s in %s", glob, dir)
    36→}

    38→// AssertNewCommits asserts that at least `atLeast` new commits exist since setup.
    39→func AssertNewCommits(t *testing.T, s *RepoState, atLeast int) {
    40→	t.Helper()
    41→	out := GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "log", "--oneline", s.HeadBefore+"..HEAD")
    42→	var lines []string
    43→	if out != "" {
    44→		lines = strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(out), "\n")
    45→	}
    46→	assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(lines), atLeast,
    47→		"expected at least %d new commit(s), got %d", atLeast, len(lines))
    48→}
    49→
    50→// WaitForCheckpoint polls until the checkpoint branch advances from its
    51→// initial state, or fails the test after timeout. Use this before any
    52→// assertions that depend on the checkpoint branch (post-commit hook is async).
    53→func WaitForCheckpoint(t *testing.T, s *RepoState, timeout time.Duration) {
    54→	t.Helper()
    55→	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
    56→	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
    57→		after := GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
    58→		if after != s.CheckpointBefore {
    59→			return
    60→		}
    61→		time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
    62→	}
    63→	t.Fatalf("checkpoint branch did not advance within %s", timeout)
    64→}
    65→
    66→// AssertCheckpointAdvanced asserts the checkpoint branch moved forward.
    67→func AssertCheckpointAdvanced(t *testing.T, s *RepoState) {
    68→	t.Helper()
    69→	after := GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
    70→	assert.NotEqual(t, s.CheckpointBefore, after, "checkpoint branch did not advance")

    99→func AssertCheckpointInLastN(t *testing.T, dir string, checkpointID string, n int) {
   100→	t.Helper()
   101→	out := GitOutput(t, dir, "log", "-n", fmt.Sprintf("%d", n),
   102→		"--format=%s", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
   103→	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(out), "\n")
   104→	require.Len(t, lines, n,
   105→		"expected %d commits on checkpoint branch, got %d", n, len(lines))
   106→	for i, line := range lines {
   107→		assert.Contains(t, line, checkpointID,
   108→			"checkpoint commit %d/%d does not mention %s: %s", i+1, n, checkpointID, line)
   109→	}
   110→}

   112→// AssertCheckpointExists asserts that the checkpoint ID is mentioned on

   114→func AssertCheckpointExists(t *testing.T, dir string, checkpointID string) {
   115→	t.Helper()
   116→	out := GitOutput(t, dir, "log", "entire/checkpoints/v1", "--grep="+checkpointID, "--oneline")
   117→	assert.NotEmpty(t, out, "checkpoint %s not found on checkpoint branch", checkpointID)
   118→
   119→	path := CheckpointPath(checkpointID) + "/metadata.json"
   120→	blob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s", path)
   121→	raw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", blob)
   122→	assert.NotEmpty(t, raw,
   123→		"checkpoint %s metadata not found at %s", checkpointID, path)
   124→}
   125→
   126→// AssertCommitLinkedToCheckpoint asserts the trailer exists AND the
   127→// checkpoint data exists on the checkpoint branch.
   128→func AssertCommitLinkedToCheckpoint(t *testing.T, dir string, ref string) {
   129→	t.Helper()

   131→	AssertCheckpointExists(t, dir, trailer)
   132→}

   144→	t.Helper()
   145→	meta := ReadCheckpointMetadata(t, dir, checkpointID)
   146→	assert.NotEmpty(t, meta.CLIVersion, "checkpoint %s: cli_version should be set", checkpointID)
   147→	assert.NotEmpty(t, meta.Strategy, "checkpoint %s: strategy should be set", checkpointID)

   149→	assert.Equal(t, checkpointID, meta.CheckpointID,

   151→}

   153→// WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom polls until the checkpoint branch advances from
   154→// the given ref, or fails the test after timeout. Use this when waiting for a
   155→// second (or subsequent) checkpoint after recording the branch position.
   156→func WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom(t *testing.T, dir string, fromRef string, timeout time.Duration) {
   157→	t.Helper()
   158→	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)

   170→func AssertNoCheckpointTrailer(t *testing.T, dir string, ref string) {

   173→	assert.Empty(t, trailer, "expected no Entire-Checkpoint trailer on %s, got %q", ref, trailer)

1→package testutil
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"fmt"
     5→	"os"
     6→	"path/filepath"
     7→	"regexp"
     8→	"strings"
     9→	"testing"
    10→	"time"
    11→
    12→	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    13→	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
    14→)
    15→
    16→var hexIDPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{12}$`)
    17→
    18→// SkipKnownIssue skips the test with a known-issue reference unless
    19→// E2E_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES=1 is set, which forces the test to run.
    20→func SkipKnownIssue(t *testing.T, issue, reason string) {
    21→	t.Helper()
    22→	if os.Getenv("E2E_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES") != "" {
    23→		t.Logf("running known issue %s (E2E_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES set): %s", issue, reason)
    24→		return
    25→	}
    26→	t.Skipf("%s: %s", issue, reason)
    27→}
    28→
    29→// AssertFileExists asserts that at least one file matches the glob pattern
    30→// relative to dir.
    31→func AssertFileExists(t *testing.T, dir string, glob string) {
    32→	t.Helper()
    33→	matches, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, glob))
    34→	require.NoError(t, err)
    35→	assert.NotEmpty(t, matches, "expected files matching %s in %s", glob, dir)
    36→}
    37→
    38→// AssertNewCommits asserts that at least `atLeast` new commits exist since setup.
    39→func AssertNewCommits(t *testing.T, s *RepoState, atLeast int) {
    40→	t.Helper()
    41→	out := GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "log", "--oneline", s.HeadBefore+"..HEAD")
    42→	var lines []string
    43→	if out != "" {
    44→		lines = strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(out), "\n")
    45→	}
    46→	assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(lines), atLeast,
    47→		"expected at least %d new commit(s), got %d", atLeast, len(lines))
    48→}
    49→
    50→// WaitForCheckpoint polls until the checkpoint branch advances from its
    51→// initial state, or fails the test after timeout. Use this before any
    52→// assertions that depend on the checkpoint branch (post-commit hook is async).
    53→func WaitForCheckpoint(t *testing.T, s *RepoState, timeout time.Duration) {
    54→	t.Helper()
    55→	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
    56→	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
    57→		after := GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
    58→		if after != s.CheckpointBefore {
    59→			return
    60→		}
    61→		time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
    62→	}
    63→	t.Fatalf("checkpoint branch did not advance within %s", timeout)
    64→}
    65→
    66→// AssertCheckpointAdvanced asserts the checkpoint branch moved forward.
    67→func AssertCheckpointAdvanced(t *testing.T, s *RepoState) {
    68→	t.Helper()
    69→	after := GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
    70→	assert.NotEqual(t, s.CheckpointBefore, after, "checkpoint branch did not advance")
    71→}
    72→
    73→// AssertCheckpointNotAdvanced asserts the checkpoint branch has NOT moved.
    74→func AssertCheckpointNotAdvanced(t *testing.T, s *RepoState) {
    75→	t.Helper()
    76→	after := GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
    77→	assert.Equal(t, s.CheckpointBefore, after, "checkpoint branch advanced unexpectedly")
    78→}
    79→
    80→// AssertCheckpointIDFormat asserts the checkpoint ID is 12 lowercase hex chars.
    81→func AssertCheckpointIDFormat(t *testing.T, checkpointID string) {
    82→	t.Helper()
    83→	assert.Regexp(t, hexIDPattern, checkpointID,
    84→		"checkpoint ID %q should be 12 lowercase hex chars", checkpointID)
    85→}
    86→
    87→// AssertHasCheckpointTrailer asserts the commit has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer,
    88→// validates its format, and returns its value.
    89→func AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t *testing.T, dir string, ref string) string {
    90→	t.Helper()
    91→	trailer := GetCheckpointTrailer(t, dir, ref)
    92→	require.NotEmpty(t, trailer, "no Entire-Checkpoint trailer on %s", ref)
    93→	AssertCheckpointIDFormat(t, trailer)
    94→	return trailer
    95→}
    96→
    97→// AssertCheckpointInLastN asserts the given checkpoint ID appears in the
    98→// last n commits on the checkpoint branch (e.g. initial + catchup).
    99→func AssertCheckpointInLastN(t *testing.T, dir string, checkpointID string, n int) {
   100→	t.Helper()
   101→	out := GitOutput(t, dir, "log", "-n", fmt.Sprintf("%d", n),
   102→		"--format=%s", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
   103→	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(out), "\n")
   104→	require.Len(t, lines, n,
   105→		"expected %d commits on checkpoint branch, got %d", n, len(lines))
   106→	for i, line := range lines {
   107→		assert.Contains(t, line, checkpointID,
   108→			"checkpoint commit %d/%d does not mention %s: %s", i+1, n, checkpointID, line)
   109→	}
   110→}
   111→
   112→// AssertCheckpointExists asserts that the checkpoint ID is mentioned on
   113→// the checkpoint branch and that its metadata.json exists in the tree.
   114→func AssertCheckpointExists(t *testing.T, dir string, checkpointID string) {
   115→	t.Helper()
   116→	out := GitOutput(t, dir, "log", "entire/checkpoints/v1", "--grep="+checkpointID, "--oneline")
   117→	assert.NotEmpty(t, out, "checkpoint %s not found on checkpoint branch", checkpointID)
   118→
   119→	path := CheckpointPath(checkpointID) + "/metadata.json"
   120→	blob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s", path)
   121→	raw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", blob)
   122→	assert.NotEmpty(t, raw,
   123→		"checkpoint %s metadata not found at %s", checkpointID, path)
   124→}
   125→
   126→// AssertCommitLinkedToCheckpoint asserts the trailer exists AND the
   127→// checkpoint data exists on the checkpoint branch.
   128→func AssertCommitLinkedToCheckpoint(t *testing.T, dir string, ref string) {
   129→	t.Helper()
   130→	trailer := AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, dir, ref)
   131→	AssertCheckpointExists(t, dir, trailer)
   132→}
   133→
   134→// AssertCheckpointHasSingleSession asserts checkpoint metadata has exactly one session.
   135→func AssertCheckpointHasSingleSession(t *testing.T, dir string, checkpointID string) {
   136→	t.Helper()
   137→	meta := ReadCheckpointMetadata(t, dir, checkpointID)
   138→	assert.Len(t, meta.Sessions, 1,
   139→		"expected 1 session in checkpoint %s, got %d", checkpointID, len(meta.Sessions))
   140→}
   141→
   142→// AssertCheckpointMetadataComplete asserts essential fields in checkpoint metadata are populated.
   143→func AssertCheckpointMetadataComplete(t *testing.T, dir string, checkpointID string) {
   144→	t.Helper()
   145→	meta := ReadCheckpointMetadata(t, dir, checkpointID)
   146→	assert.NotEmpty(t, meta.CLIVersion, "checkpoint %s: cli_version should be set", checkpointID)
   147→	assert.NotEmpty(t, meta.Strategy, "checkpoint %s: strategy should be set", checkpointID)
   148→	assert.NotEmpty(t, meta.Sessions, "checkpoint %s: should have at least 1 session", checkpointID)
   149→	assert.Equal(t, checkpointID, meta.CheckpointID,
   150→		"checkpoint metadata ID should match expected")
   151→}
   152→
   153→// WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom polls until the checkpoint branch advances from
   154→// the given ref, or fails the test after timeout. Use this when waiting for a
   155→// second (or subsequent) checkpoint after recording the branch position.
   156→func WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom(t *testing.T, dir string, fromRef string, timeout time.Duration) {
   157→	t.Helper()
   158→	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
   159→	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
   160→		after := GitOutput(t, dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
   161→		if after != fromRef {
   162→			return
   163→		}
   164→		time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
   165→	}
   166→	t.Fatalf("checkpoint branch did not advance from %s within %s", fromRef[:8], timeout)
   167→}
   168→
   169→// AssertNoCheckpointTrailer asserts the commit does NOT have an Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
   170→func AssertNoCheckpointTrailer(t *testing.T, dir string, ref string) {
   171→	t.Helper()
   172→	trailer := GetCheckpointTrailer(t, dir, ref)
   173→	assert.Empty(t, trailer, "expected no Entire-Checkpoint trailer on %s, got %q", ref, trailer)
   174→}
   175→
   176→// AssertCheckpointFilesTouched asserts the checkpoint metadata lists exactly
   177→// the expected files in files_touched (order-independent).
   178→func AssertCheckpointFilesTouched(t *testing.T, dir string, checkpointID string, expected []string) {
   179→	t.Helper()
   180→	meta := ReadCheckpointMetadata(t, dir, checkpointID)
   181→	assert.ElementsMatch(t, expected, meta.FilesTouched,
   182→		"checkpoint %s: files_touched mismatch", checkpointID)
   183→}
   184→
   185→// AssertRemoteCheckpointExists verifies the bare remote has the checkpoint
   186→// branch with the given checkpoint's metadata.json.
   187→func AssertRemoteCheckpointExists(t *testing.T, bareDir string, checkpointID string) {
   188→	t.Helper()
   189→	path := CheckpointPath(checkpointID) + "/metadata.json"
   190→	blob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s", path)
   191→	raw := gitOutputSafe(bareDir, "show", blob)
   192→	assert.NotEmpty(t, raw,
   193→		"checkpoint %s metadata not found in bare remote at %s", checkpointID, path)
   194→}
   195→
   196→// AssertCheckpointFilesTouchedContains asserts files_touched contains a
   197→// specific file path (subset check, unlike the exact-match AssertCheckpointFilesTouched).
   198→func AssertCheckpointFilesTouchedContains(t *testing.T, dir string, checkpointID string, file string) {
   199→	t.Helper()
   200→	meta := ReadCheckpointMetadata(t, dir, checkpointID)
   201→	assert.Contains(t, meta.FilesTouched, file,
   202→		"checkpoint %s: files_touched should contain %s", checkpointID, file)
   203→}
   204→
   205→// AssertDistinctSessions asserts session metadata across checkpoints has unique session IDs.
   206→func AssertDistinctSessions(t *testing.T, dir string, checkpointIDs []string) {
   207→	t.Helper()
   208→	seen := map[string]bool{}
   209→	for _, cpID := range checkpointIDs {
   210→		sm := ReadSessionMetadata(t, dir, cpID, 0)
   211→		assert.False(t, seen[sm.SessionID],
   212→			"duplicate session_id %s across checkpoints", sm.SessionID)
   213→		seen[sm.SessionID] = true
   214→	}
   215→}

    30→// SkipKnownIssue skips the test with a known-issue reference unless
    31→// E2E_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES=1 is set, which forces the test to run.
    32→func SkipKnownIssue(t *testing.T, issue, reason string) {
    33→	t.Helper()
    34→	if os.Getenv("E2E_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES") != "" {
    35→		t.Logf("running known issue %s (E2E_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES set): %s", issue, reason)
    36→		return

    41→// AssertFileExists asserts that at least one file matches the glob pattern
    42→// relative to dir.
    43→func AssertFileExists(t *testing.T, dir string, glob string) {
    44→	t.Helper()
    45→	matches, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, glob))
    46→	require.NoError(t, err)
    47→	assert.NotEmpty(t, matches, "expected files matching %s in %s", glob, dir)
    48→}
    49→
    50→// AssertNewCommits asserts that at least `atLeast` new commits exist since setup.
    51→func AssertNewCommits(t *testing.T, s *RepoState, atLeast int) {
    52→	t.Helper()
    53→	out := GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "log", "--oneline", s.HeadBefore+"..HEAD")
    54→	var lines []string
    55→	if out != "" {
    56→		lines = strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(out), "\n")
    57→	}
    58→	assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(lines), atLeast,
    59→		"expected at least %d new commit(s), got %d", atLeast, len(lines))
    60→}
    61→
    62→// WaitForCheckpoint polls until the checkpoint branch advances from its
    63→// initial state, or fails the test after timeout. Use this before any
    64→// assertions that depend on the checkpoint branch (post-commit hook is async).
    65→func WaitForCheckpoint(t *testing.T, s *RepoState, timeout time.Duration) {
    66→	t.Helper()
    67→	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
    68→	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
    69→		after := GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
    70→		if after != s.CheckpointBefore {
    71→			return
    72→		}
    73→		time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
    74→	}
    75→	t.Fatalf("checkpoint branch did not advance within %s", timeout)
    76→}
    77→
    78→// AssertCheckpointAdvanced asserts the checkpoint branch moved forward.
    79→func AssertCheckpointAdvanced(t *testing.T, s *RepoState) {
    80→	t.Helper()
    81→	after := GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

    15→func TestSubagentCommitFlow(t *testing.T) {

```go
package tests

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/entire-io/e2e-tests/testutil"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

// TestEndedSessionUserCommitsAfterExit tests that after an agent session ends
// naturally, user commits still get checkpoint trailers.
func TestEndedSessionUserCommitsAfterExit(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Create three files: ended_a.go with 'package main; func EndedA() {}', "+
				"ended_b.go with 'package main; func EndedB() {}', "+
				"ended_c.go with 'package main; func EndedC() {}'. "+
				"Create all three files, nothing else. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "ended_a.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "ended_b.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "ended_c.go")

		s.Git(t, "add", "ended_a.go", "ended_b.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add ended files A and B")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID1 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")

		cpBranchAfterFirst := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		s.Git(t, "add", "ended_c.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add ended file C")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom(t, s.Dir, cpBranchAfterFirst, 15*time.Second)
		cpID2 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")

		assert.NotEqual(t, cpID1, cpID2, "each commit should have its own checkpoint ID")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID1)
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID2)
	})
}

// TestSessionDepletedManualEditNoCheckpoint tests that once all session files
// are committed, subsequent manual edits do NOT get checkpoint trailers.
func TestSessionDepletedManualEditNoCheckpoint(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 2*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Create a file called depleted.go with content 'package main; func Depleted() {}'. "+
				"Create only this file. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "depleted.go")

		s.Git(t, "add", "depleted.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add depleted.go")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID)

		cpBranchAfterAgent := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(s.Dir, "depleted.go"),
			[]byte("package main\n\n// Manual user edit\nfunc Depleted() { return }\n"), 0o644)

		s.Git(t, "add", "depleted.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Manual edit to depleted.go")

		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterManual := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
		assert.Equal(t, cpBranchAfterAgent, cpBranchAfterManual,
			"manual edit after session depletion should not advance checkpoint branch")
		testutil.AssertNoCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
	})
}

// TestTrailerRemovalSkipsCondensation tests that when a user removes the
// Entire-Checkpoint trailer from the commit message, no condensation happens.
func TestTrailerRemovalSkipsCondensation(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 2*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Create a file called trailer_test.go with content 'package main; func TrailerTest() {}'. "+
				"Create only this file. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "trailer_test.go")

		s.Git(t, "add", "trailer_test.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", "Add trailer_test (no checkpoint)")

		testutil.AssertNoCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")

		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		testutil.AssertCheckpointNotAdvanced(t, s)
	})
}
```

```go
// TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion tests that deleting a file that was tracked
// in the session gets handled properly when committed via git rm.
func TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
			filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"),
			[]byte("package main\n\nfunc ToDelete() {}\n"), 0o644))
		s.Git(t, "add", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", "Add to_delete.go")

		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Do two things: (1) Delete the file to_delete.go using rm. "+
				"(2) Create a new file replacement.go with content 'package main; func Replacement() {}'. "+
				"Do both tasks. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		assert.NoFileExists(t, filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"))
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "replacement.go")

		s.Git(t, "add", "replacement.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add replacement")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID1 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID1)

		cpBranchAfterFirst := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		s.Git(t, "rm", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Remove to_delete.go")

		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterDeletion := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
		if cpBranchAfterDeletion != cpBranchAfterFirst {
			cpID2 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
			assert.NotEqual(t, cpID1, cpID2, "checkpoint IDs should be distinct")
			t.Logf("deletion commit got checkpoint %s (carry-forward)", cpID2)
		} else {
			t.Log("deletion commit has no checkpoint (deleted files may not carry forward)")
		}
	})
}
```

```go
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/entire-io/e2e-tests/testutil"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
```
```go
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion tests that deleting a file that was tracked
// in the session gets handled properly when committed via git rm.
func TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
			filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"),
			[]byte("package main\n\nfunc ToDelete() {}\n"), 0o644))
		s.Git(t, "add", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", "Add to_delete.go")

		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Do two things: (1) Delete the file to_delete.go using rm. "+
				"(2) Create a new file replacement.go with content 'package main; func Replacement() {}'. "+
				"Do both tasks. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		assert.NoFileExists(t, filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"))
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "replacement.go")

		s.Git(t, "add", "replacement.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add replacement")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID1 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID1)

		cpBranchAfterFirst := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		s.Git(t, "rm", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Remove to_delete.go")

		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterDeletion := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
		if cpBranchAfterDeletion != cpBranchAfterFirst {
			cpID2 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
			assert.NotEqual(t, cpID1, cpID2, "checkpoint IDs should be distinct")
			t.Logf("deletion commit got checkpoint %s (carry-forward)", cpID2)
		} else {
			t.Log("deletion commit has no checkpoint (deleted files may not carry forward)")
		}
	})
}
```

```go
// TestAgentCommitsMidTurnUserCommitsRemainder tests that when the agent commits
// some files during its turn and the user commits the rest after, both get
// valid checkpoint trailers with distinct IDs.
func TestAgentCommitsMidTurnUserCommitsRemainder(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Do these tasks in order: "+
				"(1) Create file agent_mid1.go with content 'package main; func AgentMid1() {}'. "+
				"(2) Create file agent_mid2.go with content 'package main; func AgentMid2() {}'. "+
				"(3) Run: git add agent_mid1.go agent_mid2.go && git commit -m 'Agent adds mid1 and mid2'. "+
				"(4) Create file user_remainder.go with content 'package main; func UserRemainder() {}'. "+
				"Do all tasks in order. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "agent_mid1.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "agent_mid2.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "user_remainder.go")

		testutil.AssertNewCommits(t, s, 1)

		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterAgent := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		s.Git(t, "add", "user_remainder.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add user remainder")

		testutil.WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom(t, s.Dir, cpBranchAfterAgent, 15*time.Second)
		userCpID := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		agentCpID := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD~1")

		assert.NotEqual(t, userCpID, agentCpID,
			"user and agent checkpoints should have distinct IDs")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, userCpID)
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, agentCpID)
	})
}
```

```go
package tests

import (
```

	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/entire-io/e2e-tests/testutil"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion tests that deleting a file that was tracked
// in the session gets handled properly when committed via git rm.
func TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
			filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"),
			[]byte("package main\n\nfunc ToDelete() {}\n"), 0o644))
		s.Git(t, "add", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", "Add to_delete.go")

		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Do two things: (1) Delete the file to_delete.go using rm. "+
				"(2) Create a new file replacement.go with content 'package main; func Replacement() {}'. "+
				"Do both tasks. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		assert.NoFileExists(t, filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"))
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "replacement.go")

		s.Git(t, "add", "replacement.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add replacement")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID1 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID1)

		cpBranchAfterFirst := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		s.Git(t, "rm", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Remove to_delete.go")

		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterDeletion := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
		if cpBranchAfterDeletion != cpBranchAfterFirst {
			cpID2 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
			assert.NotEqual(t, cpID1, cpID2, "checkpoint IDs should be distinct")
			t.Logf("deletion commit got checkpoint %s (carry-forward)", cpID2)
		} else {
			t.Log("deletion commit has no checkpoint (deleted files may not carry forward)")
		}
	})
}

// TestEndedSessionUserCommitsAfterExit tests that after an agent session ends
// naturally, user commits still get checkpoint trailers.
func TestEndedSessionUserCommitsAfterExit(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Create three files: ended_a.go with 'package main; func EndedA() {}', "+
				"ended_b.go with 'package main; func EndedB() {}', "+
				"ended_c.go with 'package main; func EndedC() {}'. "+
				"Create all three files, nothing else. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "ended_a.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "ended_b.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "ended_c.go")

		s.Git(t, "add", "ended_a.go", "ended_b.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add ended files A and B")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID1 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")

		cpBranchAfterFirst := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		s.Git(t, "add", "ended_c.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add ended file C")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom(t, s.Dir, cpBranchAfterFirst, 15*time.Second)
		cpID2 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")

		assert.NotEqual(t, cpID1, cpID2, "each commit should have its own checkpoint ID")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID1)
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID2)
	})
}

// TestSessionDepletedManualEditNoCheckpoint tests that once all session files
// are committed, subsequent manual edits do NOT get checkpoint trailers.
func TestSessionDepletedManualEditNoCheckpoint(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 2*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Create a file called depleted.go with content 'package main; func Depleted() {}'. "+
				"Create only this file. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "depleted.go")

		s.Git(t, "add", "depleted.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add depleted.go")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID)

		cpBranchAfterAgent := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(s.Dir, "depleted.go"),
			[]byte("package main\n\n// Manual user edit\nfunc Depleted() { return }\n"), 0o644)

		s.Git(t, "add", "depleted.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Manual edit to depleted.go")

		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterManual := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
		assert.Equal(t, cpBranchAfterAgent, cpBranchAfterManual,
			"manual edit after session depletion should not advance checkpoint branch")
		testutil.AssertNoCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
	})
}

// TestTrailerRemovalSkipsCondensation tests that when a user removes the
// Entire-Checkpoint trailer from the commit message, no condensation happens.
func TestTrailerRemovalSkipsCondensation(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 2*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Create a file called trailer_test.go with content 'package main; func TrailerTest() {}'. "+
				"Create only this file. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "trailer_test.go")

		s.Git(t, "add", "trailer_test.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", "Add trailer_test (no checkpoint)")

		testutil.AssertNoCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")

		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		testutil.AssertCheckpointNotAdvanced(t, s)
	})
}

```go
// in the session gets handled properly when committed via git rm.

	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
			filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"),
			[]byte("package main\n\nfunc ToDelete() {}\n"), 0o644))
		s.Git(t, "add", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", "Add to_delete.go")

		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Do two things: (1) Delete the file to_delete.go using rm. "+
				"(2) Create a new file replacement.go with content 'package main; func Replacement() {}'. "+
				"Do both tasks. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		assert.NoFileExists(t, filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"))
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "replacement.go")

		s.Git(t, "add", "replacement.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add replacement")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID1 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID1)

		cpBranchAfterFirst := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		s.Git(t, "rm", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Remove to_delete.go")

		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterDeletion := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
		if cpBranchAfterDeletion != cpBranchAfterFirst {
			cpID2 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
			assert.NotEqual(t, cpID1, cpID2, "checkpoint IDs should be distinct")
			t.Logf("deletion commit got checkpoint %s (carry-forward)", cpID2)
		} else {
			t.Log("deletion commit has no checkpoint (deleted files may not carry forward)")
		}
	})
}
```

```go
func TestAgentCommitsMidTurnUserCommitsRemainder(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Do these tasks in order: "+

				"(2) Create file agent_mid2.go with content 'package main; func AgentMid2() {}'. "+
				"(3) Run: git add agent_mid1.go agent_mid2.go && git commit -m 'Agent adds mid1 and mid2'. "+
				"(4) Create file user_remainder.go with content 'package main; func UserRemainder() {}'. "+
				"Do all tasks in order. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "agent_mid1.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "agent_mid2.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "user_remainder.go")

		testutil.AssertNewCommits(t, s, 1)

		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterAgent := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		s.Git(t, "add", "user_remainder.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add user remainder")

		testutil.WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom(t, s.Dir, cpBranchAfterAgent, 15*time.Second)

		agentCpID := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD~1")

			"user and agent checkpoints should have distinct IDs")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, userCpID)
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, agentCpID)
	})
}
```

```go
func TestCheckpointMetadataDeepValidation(t *testing.T) {

			CheckpointID: cpID,

}
```

All good. Both agents pass consistently. 

To answer your question — the previous pass was likely model non-determinism (Haiku sometimes gets the path right by luck). The `filepath.EvalSymlinks` fix alone wasn't sufficient because the real problem isn't symlinks — it's `t.TempDir()` creating deeply nested paths like `TestSingleSessionManualCommitClaude3076931285/001/` that confuse opencode's internal path resolution. Switching to `os.MkdirTemp` creates simple flat dirs like `e2e-repo-123456` which opencode handles correctly every time.

Want me to commit this fix?

   429→// ValidateCheckpointDeep performs comprehensive validation of checkpoint metadata
   430→// on the checkpoint branch, including transcript JSONL validity, content hash
   431→// verification, and prompt content checking.
   432→func ValidateCheckpointDeep(t *testing.T, dir string, v DeepCheckpointValidation) {
   433→	t.Helper()
   434→
   435→	// Basic metadata validation
   436→	AssertCheckpointExists(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)
   437→	AssertCheckpointMetadataComplete(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)
   438→
   439→	if v.Strategy != "" {
   440→		meta := ReadCheckpointMetadata(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)
   441→		assert.Equal(t, v.Strategy, meta.Strategy,
   442→			"checkpoint %s: strategy mismatch", v.CheckpointID)
   443→	}
   444→
   445→	if len(v.FilesTouched) > 0 {
   446→		AssertCheckpointFilesTouched(t, dir, v.CheckpointID, v.FilesTouched)
   447→	}
   448→
   449→	path := CheckpointPath(v.CheckpointID)
   450→
   451→	// Validate session metadata exists and has checkpoint_id
   452→	sessionBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/metadata.json", path)
   453→	sessionRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", sessionBlob)
   454→	if assert.NotEmpty(t, sessionRaw, "session metadata should exist at %s", sessionBlob) {
   455→		var sessionMeta map[string]any
   456→		if assert.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(sessionRaw), &sessionMeta)) {
   457→			assert.Equal(t, v.CheckpointID, sessionMeta["checkpoint_id"],
   458→				"session metadata checkpoint_id should match")
   459→			assert.NotEmpty(t, sessionMeta["created_at"], "session metadata should have created_at")
   460→		}
   461→	}
   462→
   463→	// Validate transcript is valid JSONL
   464→	transcriptBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/full.jsonl", path)
   465→	transcriptRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", transcriptBlob)
   466→	if assert.NotEmpty(t, transcriptRaw, "transcript should exist at %s", transcriptBlob) {
   467→		lines := strings.Split(transcriptRaw, "\n")
   468→		validLines := 0
   469→		for i, line := range lines {
   470→			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   471→			if line == "" {
   472→				continue
   473→			}
   474→			validLines++
   475→			var obj map[string]any
   476→			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); err != nil {
   477→				// Log but don't fail — non-Claude agents may have different formats
   478→				t.Logf("transcript line %d is not valid JSON: %v", i+1, err)
   479→			}
   480→		}
   481→		assert.Greater(t, validLines, 0, "transcript should have at least one line")
   482→
   483→		for _, expected := range v.ExpectedTranscriptContent {
   484→			assert.Contains(t, transcriptRaw, expected,
   485→				"transcript should contain %q", expected)
   486→		}
   487→
   488→		// Validate content hash
   489→		hashBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/content_hash.txt", path)
   490→		hashRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", hashBlob)
   491→		if hashRaw != "" {
   492→			hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(transcriptRaw))
   493→			expectedHash := "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])
   494→			assert.Equal(t, expectedHash, strings.TrimSpace(hashRaw),
   495→				"content hash should match transcript SHA-256")
   496→		}
   497→	}
   498→
   499→	// Validate prompt.txt if expected prompts specified
   500→	if len(v.ExpectedPrompts) > 0 {
   501→		promptBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/prompt.txt", path)
   502→		promptRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", promptBlob)
   503→		for _, expected := range v.ExpectedPrompts {
   504→			assert.Contains(t, promptRaw, expected,
   505→				"prompt.txt should contain %q", expected)
   506→		}
   507→	}
   508→}

   615→package agents

   626→
   627→type openCodeAgent struct {
   628→	model   string
   629→	timeout time.Duration
   630→}
   631→
   632→func init() {
   633→	if _, err := exec.LookPath("opencode"); err != nil {
   634→		return // don't register if not installed
   635→	}
   636→	model := os.Getenv("E2E_OPENCODE_MODEL")
   637→	if model == "" {
   638→		model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
   639→	}
   640→	Register(&openCodeAgent{model: model, timeout: 2 * time.Minute})
   641→}
   642→
   643→func (a *openCodeAgent) Name() string            { return "opencode" }
   644→func (a *openCodeAgent) EntireAgent() string      { return "opencode" }
   645→func (a *openCodeAgent) PromptPattern() string    { return `\$` }
   646→func (a *openCodeAgent) TimeoutMultiplier() float64 { return 2.0 }
   647→
   648→func (a *openCodeAgent) RunPrompt(ctx context.Context, dir string, prompt string, opts ...Option) (Output, error) {
   649→	cfg := &runConfig{}
   650→	for _, o := range opts {
   651→		o(cfg)
   652→	}
   653→
   654→	model := a.model
   655→	if cfg.Model != "" {
   656→		model = cfg.Model
   657→	}
   658→
   659→	args := []string{"run"}
   660→	if model != "" {
   661→		args = append(args, "--model", model)
   662→	}
   663→	args = append(args, prompt)
   664→
   665→	timeout := a.timeout
   666→	if envTimeout := os.Getenv("E2E_TIMEOUT"); envTimeout != "" {
   667→		if parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(envTimeout); err == nil {
   668→			timeout = parsed
   669→		}
   670→	}
   671→
   672→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
   673→	defer cancel()
   674→
   675→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "opencode", args...)
   676→	cmd.Dir = dir
   677→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0")

```go
package tests

import (
	"context"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/entire-io/e2e-tests/testutil"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

// TestEndedSessionUserCommitsAfterExit tests that after an agent session ends
// naturally, user commits still get checkpoint trailers. This exercises the
// session ENDED + user commit path.
func TestEndedSessionUserCommitsAfterExit(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		// Agent creates 3 files — session ends when agent exits
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Create three files: ended_a.go with 'package main; func EndedA() {}', "+
				"ended_b.go with 'package main; func EndedB() {}', "+
				"ended_c.go with 'package main; func EndedC() {}'. "+
				"Create all three files, nothing else. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "ended_a.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "ended_b.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "ended_c.go")

		// User commits A and B together
		s.Git(t, "add", "ended_a.go", "ended_b.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add ended files A and B")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID1 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")

		// Capture checkpoint branch ref for polling second checkpoint
		cpBranchAfterFirst := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		// User commits C separately
		s.Git(t, "add", "ended_c.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add ended file C")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom(t, s.Dir, cpBranchAfterFirst, 15*time.Second)
		cpID2 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")

		// Checkpoint IDs must be distinct
		assert.NotEqual(t, cpID1, cpID2, "each commit should have its own checkpoint ID")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID1)
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID2)
	})
}
```

```go
// TestSessionDepletedManualEditNoCheckpoint tests that once all session files
// are committed, subsequent manual edits do NOT get checkpoint trailers.
func TestSessionDepletedManualEditNoCheckpoint(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 2*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		// Agent creates a file
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Create a file called depleted.go with content 'package main; func Depleted() {}'. "+
				"Create only this file. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "depleted.go")

		// User commits the agent's file → gets checkpoint
		s.Git(t, "add", "depleted.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add depleted.go")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID)

		cpBranchAfterAgent := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		// User manually edits the file (not from agent)
		os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(s.Dir, "depleted.go"),
			[]byte("package main\n\n// Manual user edit\nfunc Depleted() { return }\n"), 0o644)

		// User commits the manual edit
		s.Git(t, "add", "depleted.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Manual edit to depleted.go")

		// Wait briefly, then verify no new checkpoint
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterManual := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
		assert.Equal(t, cpBranchAfterAgent, cpBranchAfterManual,
			"manual edit after session depletion should not advance checkpoint branch")
		testutil.AssertNoCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
	})
}
```

```go
// TestTrailerRemovalSkipsCondensation tests that when a user removes the
// Entire-Checkpoint trailer from the commit message, no condensation happens.
func TestTrailerRemovalSkipsCondensation(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 2*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		// Agent creates a file
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Create a file called trailer_test.go with content 'package main; func TrailerTest() {}'. "+
				"Create only this file. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "trailer_test.go")

		// User commits, but uses --no-verify to bypass hooks (simulating trailer removal).
		// The prepare-commit-msg hook would normally add the trailer; skipping it
		// means the commit has no trailer, same effect as the user editing it out.
		s.Git(t, "add", "trailer_test.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", "Add trailer_test (no checkpoint)")

		// Verify commit has no trailer
		testutil.AssertNoCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")

		// Wait briefly, then verify checkpoint branch did not advance
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		testutil.AssertCheckpointNotAdvanced(t, s)
	})
}
```

```go
package tests

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/entire-io/e2e-tests/testutil"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion tests that deleting a file that was tracked
// in the session gets handled properly when committed via git rm.
func TestDeletedFilesCommitDeletion(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		// Pre-seed a file that the agent will delete
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
			filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"),
			[]byte("package main\n\nfunc ToDelete() {}\n"), 0o644))
		s.Git(t, "add", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", "Add to_delete.go")

		// Agent deletes it and creates a replacement
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Do two things: (1) Delete the file to_delete.go using rm. "+
				"(2) Create a new file replacement.go with content 'package main; func Replacement() {}'. "+
				"Do both tasks. Do not commit. "+
				"Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		// to_delete.go should be gone, replacement.go should exist
		assert.NoFileExists(t, filepath.Join(s.Dir, "to_delete.go"))
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "replacement.go")

		// Commit the replacement file
		s.Git(t, "add", "replacement.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add replacement")
		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpID1 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, cpID1)

		cpBranchAfterFirst := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		// Commit the deletion via git rm
		s.Git(t, "rm", "to_delete.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Remove to_delete.go")

		// Check if deletion got a checkpoint — this is soft validation
		// (deleted files may or may not carry forward depending on CLI behavior)
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterDeletion := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
		if cpBranchAfterDeletion != cpBranchAfterFirst {
			cpID2 := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
			assert.NotEqual(t, cpID1, cpID2, "checkpoint IDs should be distinct")
			t.Logf("deletion commit got checkpoint %s (carry-forward)", cpID2)
		} else {
			t.Log("deletion commit has no checkpoint (deleted files may not carry forward)")
		}
	})
}
```

```go
// TestAgentCommitsMidTurnUserCommitsRemainder tests that when the agent commits
// some files during its turn and the user commits the rest after, both get
// valid checkpoint trailers with distinct IDs.
func TestAgentCommitsMidTurnUserCommitsRemainder(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
		// Agent creates 3 files and commits 2 mid-turn
		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
			"Do these tasks in order: "+
				"(1) Create file agent_mid1.go with content 'package main; func AgentMid1() {}'. "+
				"(2) Create file agent_mid2.go with content 'package main; func AgentMid2() {}'. "+
				"(3) Run: git add agent_mid1.go agent_mid2.go && git commit -m 'Agent adds mid1 and mid2'. "+
				"(4) Create file user_remainder.go with content 'package main; func UserRemainder() {}'. "+
				"Do all tasks in order. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the changes.")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
		}

		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "agent_mid1.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "agent_mid2.go")
		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "user_remainder.go")

		// Agent should have committed mid-turn
		testutil.AssertNewCommits(t, s, 1)

		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
		cpBranchAfterAgent := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")

		// User commits the remaining file
		s.Git(t, "add", "user_remainder.go")
		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add user remainder")

		testutil.WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom(t, s.Dir, cpBranchAfterAgent, 15*time.Second)
		userCpID := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
		agentCpID := testutil.AssertHasCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD~1")

		assert.NotEqual(t, userCpID, agentCpID,
			"user and agent checkpoints should have distinct IDs")
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, userCpID)
		testutil.AssertCheckpointExists(t, s.Dir, agentCpID)
	})
}
```

### Task 7: Add `ValidateCheckpointDeep` assertion helper

The CLI repo's `ValidateCheckpoint` does comprehensive validation: transcript JSONL, content_hash SHA-256, prompt.txt. Port this as a deeper validation helper.

**Files:**

**Step 1: Add the helper**

Add to `testutil/assertions.go`:

```go
// ValidateCheckpointDeep performs comprehensive validation of checkpoint metadata
// on the checkpoint branch, including transcript JSONL validity, content hash
// verification, and prompt content checking.
func ValidateCheckpointDeep(t *testing.T, dir string, v DeepCheckpointValidation) {
	t.Helper()

	// Basic metadata validation
	AssertCheckpointExists(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)
	AssertCheckpointMetadataComplete(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)

	if v.Strategy != "" {
		meta := ReadCheckpointMetadata(t, dir, v.CheckpointID)
		assert.Equal(t, v.Strategy, meta.Strategy,
			"checkpoint %s: strategy mismatch", v.CheckpointID)
	}

	if len(v.FilesTouched) > 0 {
		AssertCheckpointFilesTouched(t, dir, v.CheckpointID, v.FilesTouched)
	}

	path := CheckpointPath(v.CheckpointID)

	// Validate session metadata exists and has checkpoint_id
	sessionBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/metadata.json", path)
	sessionRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", sessionBlob)
	if assert.NotEmpty(t, sessionRaw, "session metadata should exist at %s", sessionBlob) {
		var sessionMeta map[string]any
		if assert.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(sessionRaw), &sessionMeta)) {
			assert.Equal(t, v.CheckpointID, sessionMeta["checkpoint_id"],
				"session metadata checkpoint_id should match")
			assert.NotEmpty(t, sessionMeta["created_at"], "session metadata should have created_at")
		}
	}

	// Validate transcript is valid JSONL
	transcriptBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/full.jsonl", path)
	transcriptRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", transcriptBlob)
	if assert.NotEmpty(t, transcriptRaw, "transcript should exist at %s", transcriptBlob) {
		lines := strings.Split(transcriptRaw, "\n")
		validLines := 0
		for i, line := range lines {
			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
			if line == "" {
				continue
			}
			validLines++
			var obj map[string]any
			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); err != nil {
				// Log but don't fail — non-Claude agents may have different formats
				t.Logf("transcript line %d is not valid JSON: %v", i+1, err)
			}
		}
		assert.Greater(t, validLines, 0, "transcript should have at least one line")

		for _, expected := range v.ExpectedTranscriptContent {
			assert.Contains(t, transcriptRaw, expected,
				"transcript should contain %q", expected)
		}

		// Validate content hash
		hashBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/content_hash.txt", path)
		hashRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", hashBlob)
		if hashRaw != "" {
			hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(transcriptRaw))
			expectedHash := "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])
			assert.Equal(t, expectedHash, strings.TrimSpace(hashRaw),
				"content hash should match transcript SHA-256")
		}
	}

	// Validate prompt.txt if expected prompts specified
	if len(v.ExpectedPrompts) > 0 {
		promptBlob := fmt.Sprintf("entire/checkpoints/v1:%s/0/prompt.txt", path)
		promptRaw := gitOutputSafe(dir, "show", promptBlob)
		for _, expected := range v.ExpectedPrompts {
			assert.Contains(t, promptRaw, expected,
				"prompt.txt should contain %q", expected)
		}
	}
}
```

## Phase 3: Add OpenCode Agent Support

### Task 9: Add OpenCode agent

**Files:**
- Create: `agents/opencode.go`

**Step 1: Write the agent**

```go
package agents

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

type openCodeAgent struct {
	model   string
	timeout time.Duration
}

func init() {
	if _, err := exec.LookPath("opencode"); err != nil {
		return // don't register if not installed
	}
	model := os.Getenv("E2E_OPENCODE_MODEL")
	if model == "" {
		model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
	}
	Register(&openCodeAgent{model: model, timeout: 2 * time.Minute})
}

func (a *openCodeAgent) Name() string            { return "opencode" }
func (a *openCodeAgent) EntireAgent() string      { return "opencode" }
func (a *openCodeAgent) PromptPattern() string    { return `\$` }
func (a *openCodeAgent) TimeoutMultiplier() float64 { return 2.0 }

func (a *openCodeAgent) RunPrompt(ctx context.Context, dir string, prompt string, opts ...Option) (Output, error) {
	cfg := &runConfig{}
	for _, o := range opts {
		o(cfg)
	}

	model := a.model
	if cfg.Model != "" {
		model = cfg.Model
	}

	args := []string{"run"}
	if model != "" {
		args = append(args, "--model", model)
	}
	args = append(args, prompt)

	timeout := a.timeout
	if envTimeout := os.Getenv("E2E_TIMEOUT"); envTimeout != "" {
		if parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(envTimeout); err == nil {
			timeout = parsed
		}
	}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
	defer cancel()

	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "opencode", args...)
	cmd.Dir = dir
	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0")

	var stdout, stderr strings.Builder
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
	cmd.Stderr = &stderr

	err := cmd.Run()
	out := Output{
		Command: fmt.Sprintf("opencode %s", strings.Join(args, " ")),
		Stdout:  stdout.String(),
		Stderr:  stderr.String(),
	}

	if err != nil {
		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
			out.ExitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
		} else {
			out.ExitCode = -1
		}
		return out, err
	}

	return out, nil
}

func (a *openCodeAgent) StartSession(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Session, error) {
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("opencode: interactive sessions not supported")
}
```

In /Users/alex/workspace/cli/e2e/, I need to:

1. Replace all import paths from `github.com/entire-io/e2e-tests/` to `github.com/entireio/cli/e2e/` in all .go files under the e2e/ directory.

2. Add `//go:build e2e` as the FIRST line (before `package`) of every `*_test.go` file in `e2e/tests/`. There should be a blank line between the build tag and the package declaration.

Do NOT modify files in `e2e/agents/`, `e2e/entire/`, or `e2e/testutil/` for the build tag — only the test files in `e2e/tests/`.

Run these commands:

```bash
# 1. Update import paths in all Go files
cd /Users/alex/workspace/cli
find e2e -name '*.go' -exec sed -i '' 's|github.com/entire-io/e2e-tests/|github.com/entireio/cli/e2e/|g' {} +

# 2. Add //go:build e2e to test files in tests/ 
for f in e2e/tests/*_test.go; do
  # Check if build tag already exists
  if ! head -1 "$f" | grep -q '//go:build'; then
    # Prepend build tag with blank line
    printf '//go:build e2e\n\n' | cat - "$f" > "$f.tmp" && mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
  fi
done

# 3. Verify no old import paths remain
echo "=== Remaining old imports ==="
grep -r 'entire-io/e2e-tests' e2e/ || echo "None found (good)"

# 4. Verify build tags
echo "=== Build tags in test files ==="
for f in e2e/tests/*_test.go; do
  echo "$f: $(head -1 "$f")"
done
```

[tools]
# Please also keep the version aligned in the go.mod file
go = { version = '1.25.6', postinstall = "go install github.com/go-delve/delve/cmd/dlv@latest" }
golangci-lint = '2.8.0'
shellcheck = 'latest'

[tasks.fmt]
description = "Run gofmt"
run = "gofmt -s -w ."

[tasks.test]
description = "Run tests"
run = "go test ./..."

[tasks."test:integration"]
description = "Run integration tests"
run = "go test -tags=integration ./cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/..."

[tasks."test:ci"]
description = "Run all tests (unit + integration) with race detection"
run = "go test -tags=integration -race ./..."

[tasks.build]
description = "Build the CLI"
run = """
VERSION=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo "dev")
COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/buildinfo.Version=${VERSION} -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/buildinfo.Commit=${COMMIT}" -o entire ./cmd/entire
"""

[tasks."build:all"]
description = "Build for all platforms using goreleaser"
run = "goreleaser build --snapshot --clean"

[tasks."completions"]
description = "generate entire shell completions"
quiet = true
run = """
rm -rf completions
mkdir completions
for sh in bash zsh fish; do
    go run ./cmd/entire/main.go completion "$sh" >"completions/entire.$sh"
done
"""

[tasks.dup]
description = "Check for code duplication (threshold 50, with summary)"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Create temp files with proper extensions (works on both Linux and macOS)
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
config="$tmpdir/config.yaml"
json_out="$tmpdir/output.json"

cat > "$config" << 'YAML'
version: "2"
linters:
  default: none
  enable: [dupl]
  settings:
    dupl:
      threshold: 50
YAML

# Run with JSON output for summary, text output for details
golangci-lint run -c "$config" --new=false --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0 \
  --output.json.path="$json_out" --output.text.path=/dev/stderr ./... 2>&1 || true

# Print summary grouped by file
echo ""
echo "=== Duplication Summary (by file) ==="
if command -v jq &>/dev/null && [ -s "$json_out" ]; then
  jq -r '.Issues // [] | group_by(.Pos.Filename) | map({file: (.[0].Pos.Filename | split("/") | .[-1]), count: length}) | sort_by(-.count) | .[] | "  " + (.count|tostring) + " " + .file' "$json_out" 2>/dev/null || echo "  (no issues)"
else
  echo "  (install jq for summary)"
fi

rm -rf "$tmpdir"
"""

[tasks."dup:staged"]
description = "Check duplication in staged files only (threshold 75, same as CI)"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Get staged Go files, preserving paths with spaces using null delimiters throughout
if ! git diff --cached --name-only -z --diff-filter=ACM | grep -z '\\.go$' | grep -zq .; then
  echo "No staged Go files to check"
  exit 0
fi
echo "Checking staged files for duplication..."
git diff --cached --name-only -z --diff-filter=ACM | grep -z '\\.go$' | xargs -0 golangci-lint run --enable-only dupl --new=false --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0
"""

[tasks.bench]
description = "Run all benchmarks"
run = '''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

output=$(go test -bench=. -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=10m ./... 2>&1)

# Print non-benchmark lines (ok, PASS, etc.) to stderr
echo "$output" | grep -v '^Benchmark' >&2

# Format benchmark lines as a table with headers using column
bench_lines=$(echo "$output" | grep '^Benchmark' || true)
if [ -n "$bench_lines" ]; then
  {
    echo "BENCHMARK ITERS MS/OP NS/OP B/OP ALLOCS/OP"
    echo "--------- ----- ----- ----- ---- ---------"
    # Strip unit suffixes and add ms/op column (ns/op / 1000000)
    echo "$bench_lines" | sed 's/ ns\/op//g; s/ B\/op//g; s/ allocs\/op//g; s/ transcript_bytes//g' \
      | awk '{printf "%s %s %.2f %s %s %s\n", $1, $2, $3/1000000, $3, $4, $5}'
  } | column -t
fi
'''

[tasks."test:e2e"]
description = "Run E2E tests with real agent calls (requires claude CLI)"
# -count=1 disables test caching since E2E tests call real external agents
run = "go test -tags=e2e -count=1 -timeout=30m -v ./cmd/entire/cli/e2e_test/..."

[tasks."test:e2e:claude"]
description = "Run E2E tests with Claude Code (haiku model)"
run = "E2E_AGENT=claude-code go test -tags=e2e -count=1 -timeout=30m -v ./cmd/entire/cli/e2e_test/..."

[tasks."test:e2e:gemini"]
description = "Run E2E tests with Gemini CLI (sequential to avoid rate limits)"
run = "E2E_AGENT=gemini go test -tags=e2e -count=1 -parallel 1 -timeout=30m -v ./cmd/entire/cli/e2e_test/..."

[tasks."test:e2e:opencode"]
description = "Run E2E tests with OpenCode"
run = "E2E_AGENT=opencode go test -tags=e2e -count=1 -timeout=30m -v ./cmd/entire/cli/e2e_test/..."
